title: Cartridge Rate from Pump Insulin Use: Clinical Supply Guide for the Insulin Pump Program
content:
The cartridge rate of a cartridge or reservoir refill on an Insulin Pump Program — the cartridges allowed per 30 days — follows the customer's dispensing on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program, that is, on the customer's active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump, whose pump insulin item is J1817 on the Insulin Pharmacy Medicare Part B Pump Insulin Program and rapid-acting 10 mL vials on any other tier:

1. Where the customer holds such an active program and its pump insulin item was dispensed under it in the six months before the ship date, the standard cartridge rate is replaced with the lesser of the ordered rate and the cartridges the daily pump insulin needs per 30 days: 30 times the daily pump insulin divided by the usable fill per cartridge, rounded up to a whole cartridge and never fewer than one cartridge for every stability period of 3 days in 30 days, rounded up — that is, never fewer than 10.
2. Where the customer holds such a program but that item was not dispensed under it in those six months, it is replaced with the tier's reservoirs per 30 days.
3. Otherwise the standard cartridge rate stands.

A dispensing counts as in the six months before the ship date when its date is later than the same day of the month six months before the ship date.

| Hypothetical case | Cartridge rate |
|---|---|
| Daily pump insulin 70 units, usable fill 200 units, ordered rate 15 | 2,100 divided by 200 is 10.5, rounded up to 11; replaced with the lesser of 15 and 11, which is 11 |
| Daily pump insulin 60 units, usable fill 300 units, ordered rate 15 | 1,800 divided by 300 is 6, held at 10; replaced with 10 |
| Item not dispensed in 6 months; tier with 15 cartridges per 30 days | replaced with 15 |
| No insulin pharmacy program delivering by insulin pump | the standard cartridge rate stands |
